chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: The film 'St. Louis Blues' and her part in it
summary: She describes the picture, the cast, Matty Malneck's band, and being discovered washing clothes outside her cabin.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: when the picture was released, on the stage, with the picture. By this time, the record was out and everything was great.
That picture was something that was not much to be desired.
(Inaudible).
Yeah. I figured it was one of the naked-as-you-go pictures. The main purpose was to get Dorothy Lamour out of the sarong, or out that plot. I think we had a skeleton of a plot. But anyway --
You mean out of it and into something else or just out of it?

Out of it. Period: Lloyd Nolan was the captain of this boat. And they were riding down the Mississippi, and they got stranded on somebody's lawn. Tito Guizar, who had this tobacco plantation -- he happened to be down in South America, and they decided that they would put on a show to raise some money to get this boat off of Tito Guizar's

lawn, see.
So, in the meantime, they went around rounding up talent. They discovered Matty Malneck and his group playing around there in the streets, you know, for pennies.
And they sort of went out --
Matty Malneck is the musical -- Malneck.
Yeah, Matty Malneck.
M-a-l-n-e-c-k --
Um hum.
Was the musical director.
That's right.
And he had -- for the picture, he had a combination of harp, violin, accordion, bass, and I guess drums or trumpet. Manny Klein was on trumpet.
He'd also been on your first recording session.
That's right.
So they did the little arrangements and they appeared in the picture too.

And, of course, they discovered me outside of my cabin washing clothes and singing the St. Louis Blues. And I think this is when the NAACP decided that there weren't going to be no more stereotypes for Blacks in movies.
That didn't immediately come to pass either, did it?

No, no. But that was the last straw, because I was supposed to be discovered and brought on this boat.

And Lloyd Nolan is the captain -- he was going to teach me to sing 'Lock Lomond,' a Scot song, and he's going to teach me this Russian song.

So I got into sort of a hassle with the director there because he came to me and he said that I didn't have -- I wasn't giving enough of the dialect -- the southern dialect.

So I got a little annoyed. I mean, I could've hammed it up a little bit, but... I said, 'Look, it doesn't make sense to me for me to be talking a dialect one minute and singing Ochi Chornia in Russian the next minute.'
